places.title: Islamia College Peshawar
places.body: Founded in 1913, Islamia College is an architectural masterpiece of red-brick Islamic-colonial design, crowned with elegant cupolas, clock towers, arched arcades, and sprawling manicured lawns flanked by cypress trees.

places.title: Qissa Khwani Bazaar
places.body: The legendary 'Street of Storytellers' in Peshawar's Old City, famed for traditional multi-story carved wooden havelis, steaming brass samovars of Peshawari Kahwa green tea, copper artisans, and vibrant fabric merchants.

places.title: Zu Peshawar (BRT)
places.body: Peshawar's 27-kilometer modern rapid transit network with clean electric-diesel hybrid buses, raised island stations, glass fare turnstiles, illuminated passenger information displays, and dedicated level-boarding bridges.

places.title: Sethi House & Mohallah
places.body: Built in 1884 by wealthy merchant traders, Sethi Haveli showcases Central Asian Bukhara-inspired architecture, intricate deodar wooden jharokas, hand-carved balconies, a courtyard with a turquoise fountain, and a sunken basement.

places.title: All Saints Church
places.body: Consecrated in 1883 inside Kohati Gate, this historic church is internationally famous for its unique Saracenic/Mughal mosque-like architecture—featuring minarets, cupolas, pointed arches, and Christian scriptures inscribed in Persian, Arabic, and Urdu calligraphy.

places.title: Jahaz Chowk (Aircraft Roundabout)
places.body: An iconic urban roundabout crowned by a mounted fighter jet monument surrounded by concentric marigold beds, bustling with continuous flows of white cars, yellow taxis, green rickshaws, and pedestrians crossing towards the Cantt.

places.title: Bala Hisar Fort
places.body: Standing on a commanding high mound overlooking the entire Peshawar valley for centuries, Bala Hisar ('High Fort') features massive rammed-earth and brick ramparts, defensive bastions, and a museum of Frontier Corps and Pashtun history.

situations.title: Locating the Sir Sahibzada Abdul Qayyum Hall
situations.body: Dawood Kaka must find the historic lecture hall in the east quadrangle for a 10:00 AM centenary lecture. The symmetrical red-brick arches look identical.

situations.title: Boarding the Direct Express Line During Peak Hour
situations.body: Bilal arrives on the platform where two different buses stop at the same bay: Route 01 (All Stops) and Route 02 (Express Direct). He needs Route 02.

situations.title: Ordering Custom Green Tea with Dietary Needs
situations.body: Mehwish wants to order signature Peshawari Kahwa with cardamom and crushed almonds, but explicitly without added sugar due to diabetes.

situations.title: Purchasing a Single Trip Token with Cash
situations.body: Parveen Bibi is selecting 'Hayatabad Mall' on the touch kiosk and inserting two crisp 50-rupee notes into the bill validator.

barriers.title: Low-Contrast Symmetrical Architecture & Lack of Landmarks
barriers.body: All corridors look uniform. The historic wooden door plaques feature carved dark brown letters on dark brown timber with zero visual contrast, positioned 2.5 meters above ground level.

barriers.title: Silent Bus Arrival & Digital Display Only
barriers.body: The electronic destination screen on the bus windshield updates in LED pixels, but the bus makes almost zero engine noise (electric-hybrid) and there is no station audio broadcast specifying which route has docked.

barriers.title: Verbal-Only Shouted Order Culture
barriers.body: The tea house has no written menu or prices. The head tea-master shouts orders to boys at the stoves behind boiling steam, and calls out names when tea is ready.

barriers.title: 15-Second Aggressive Session Timeout
barriers.body: While Parveen unzips her purse to extract the cash, the kiosk counts down 15 seconds without audio warning. The session abruptly cancels, resets the screen to the Urdu/English landing page, and ejects nothing.
